title: The derived adjunction $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ on module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. The adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ on module objects
([def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]) induces an adjunction

$$
Lf^*\dashv Rf_*
$$

between the total left derived functor of $f^*$, computed on K-flat resolutions in
$\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$ ([lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso]), and the total right
derived functor of $f_*$, computed on K-injective resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, use the small site of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $C_T=\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. By [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $C_T$ is Grothendieck abelian and closed symmetric monoidal. Here $\Ab$ has its tensor product over $\mathbf Z$, not the cartesian product.

source.place: Parts 3–4: sheaf and module category structures and flat covers; structural hypotheses assembled using the cited individual statements

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] to $\Ab$, using [lem-sfb-abelian-functorial-flat-resolution]. This gives functorial flat resolutions in $C_T$. Its tensor is additive since each tensor functor preserves finite biproducts: colimit preservation is [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor].

source.place: Parts 3–4: sheaf and module category structures and flat covers; structural hypotheses assembled using the cited individual statements

proof.text: The ring $\Lambda_T$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For its module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] to step 1, and [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] to step 2. Thus $M_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ is closed symmetric monoidal, Grothendieck abelian, and has functorial flat resolutions.

source.place: Parts 3–4: sheaf and module category structures and flat covers; structural hypotheses assembled using the cited individual statements

proof.text: Closedness and symmetry make either fixed-factor tensor on $M_T$ a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], hence is additive by preservation of finite biproducts. Grothendieck abelian gives countable coproducts and exact filtered colimits; $\mathbf Z$ is filtered since $\max(i,j)$ bounds $i,j$. These are all the structural hypotheses of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

source.place: Parts 3–4: sheaf and module category structures and flat covers; structural hypotheses assembled using the cited individual statements

proof.text: Take $F=f^*$ and $G=f_*$, additive by [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and [def-sfb-module-lower-star], with $F\dashv G$ from [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. By [lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso], $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Apply [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] using steps 3–4: $LF$ exists on K-flat resolutions in $M_Y$, and $RG$ on K-injective resolutions in $M_X$.

source.place: Proof: specialize the general derived adjunction to the full module functors

proof.text: The derived-adjunction clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] now gives $LF\dashv RG$. Define $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ to be this specialization; its functors are the total derived functors of the full module functors $F,G$ of step 5, with the stated resolutions.

source.place: Proof: specialize the general derived adjunction to the full module functors

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q31-c2936d750 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full; review.md has the details. The item statement is verbatim the main-20261015 blueprint statement and is not weakened. The coefficient category is module objects over Λ_X=p_X^*Λ in Sh(X_proét,Ab) with ⊗_Z, as in the unit and in the layer-B row of sk-def-sfb-derived-categories; no base-change morphism is involved. The human's return asked for a finer split, and the delivery answers it: six steps of about 2100 characters in total, the longest about 420. Steps 1–4 assemble Parts 3–4 of sk-prop-sfb-module-category. Part 3 comes from that unit's own nodes: modobj-grothendieck, symmetric tensor, internal hom and modobj flat resolutions. Part 4 comes from the generic theorems lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck and lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution together with the new Ab coefficient lemma; no existing node realizes Part 4 for sheaves. Every hypothesis of every cited statement holds where it is used. In step 4, the left-derived bullet of sk-def-sfb-derived-categories is checked item by item: additive tensor, countable coproducts, exact Z-colimits preserved by tensoring, and functorial flat resolutions. Steps 5–6 apply the K-injective and K-flat derived-functor clauses and the derived-adjunction clause to the full composite module functors. Those composites are the same functors as in def-sfb-module-upper-star, def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction and lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso. There is no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. The new node lem-sfb-abelian-functorial-flat-resolution is true: Z[M]→M is natural and surjective, and Z[M] is flat because Z[M]⊗A≅⊕A. I tested it on M=0 and on torsion M. It is statement-only and self-contained (B1–B4, B7, B9 hold). It is not a clause of the parent. It is not a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-module-functorial-flat-resolution, lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions, lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution and lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-flat-separator all assume the coefficient input rather than supply it, and lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover belongs to another unit and would need an identification with sheaves on a point. The live AddCommGrpCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution (Basic.lean:150, through RingObjects/Ab.lean:289–291, no sorry in either file) states the node exactly and is recorded as an attachment candidate. I accept the 14 declared tool_uses as generic black-box inputs. Advisories only: step 2 could list Ab's hypotheses explicitly, and the new node's source place could say 'coefficient case of the Part 4 free-sheaf argument'.
